There is the possibility of cross-resistance develop- ing between brivudine and aciclovir because of some similar fea- tures in their mode of action (see p.863). Brivudine is given orally in the treatment of herpes zoster (p.855) in a dose of 125 mg daily for 7 days. There have been instanc- es of acute renal failure after only 1 or 2 doses, and some fatalities. Low plasma-bicarbonate concentra- tions and metabolic acidosis, sometimes associated with proximal tubule injury and renal wasting syn- drome (including Fanconi’s syndrome) or with liver dysfunction and pancreatitis, have been reported.
